title: The Berry Brothers act at the Paramount with Tommy Ladnier
summary: Zutty and Tommy Ladnier played the pit for the Berry Brothers act at the Paramount, then Brooklyn and Providence, and Joe Jordan used the union delegate threat to get the locked pit doors opened.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Zutty done a lot of show drumming like the Berry Brothers.

Yes, now this is another thing he says, during the early thirties worked for several other leaders including Bubber Miley and Otto Toby Hardwick together with Tommy Ladnier accompanied the Berry Brothers dancing act.
Ladnier did, we did that at the Paramount Theater. And we played two weeks here at the Paramount, then we went to Brooklyn and played two weeks. Then we went to Providence, Rhode Island.
No, we were in the pit.

In the pit. And Mike ( VASSO ?) he was so nice to us you know. And a trumpet player by the name of MERVE ? Steinberg he was nice to us. Because at one time before the first show, after the pit band went in, then they had the doors all locked. And Joe Jordan was the delegate that, So Joe Jordan said, well if they don't open those doors down there, he say, you all come out and jump from the stage to the pit, see. And I think it was Whiteman was the manager of the theater, the Paramount Theater.
So when they found that out man, they opened those doors so Tommy Ladnier and I could get down in that pit. It seemed that they had to bring the pit down again for us to go back in there.
